question: access

request.from: a cloud container in a datacenter network, egress 205.188.204.187
request.body: one keyless tools/call of aws___search_documentation, the prefixed name this endpoint's own tools/list serves, with the same search_phrase argument as the refused unprefixed call, jsonrpc 2.0, Accept application/json and text/event-stream

decoded.what-it-answered: HTTP/2 200, content-type application/json, 7323 bytes, result.isError false, content carrying ranked documentation results, the first titled "What is AWS Lambda?". Read at 18:04:27Z, 28 seconds after the refused unprefixed call.
decoded.why-this-record-exists: it is the CONTROL for p-20260930-aws-knowledge-mcp-unprefixed-name-refused. Same endpoint, same argument, same minute; the only difference is the aws___ prefix. Without it, the refusal would be consistent with a broken or key-gated tool, and the finding would not be about NAMES. Filed on its own because a probe is one request, and the record it controls names it.
decoded.what-it-establishes: the five tools this endpoint serves work keyless and free for an anonymous caller, exactly as the vendor documents. The defect in the sibling records is confined to the tool names written into the descriptions.
decoded.and-what-it-does-not-establish: nothing about a rate limit. This request and the two before it were spaced 25 seconds apart precisely because this endpoint answered 429 to a denser sweep earlier the same day (p-20260930-aws-knowledge-mcp-anonymous-429).
decoded.why-this-record-is-one-request: this record is ONE request. The previous head of this pull request combined a tools/list, five refused tools/call requests and one control call under a single observed.status, which the registry's reviewer held, rightly: the probe schema's title reads "One unauthenticated, unpaid request and what it answered". The comparison across those requests is now carried by named sibling records and by prose, not by one status field.

finding: Calling aws___search_documentation on the AWS Knowledge MCP endpoint, keyless and with the same argument that the unprefixed search_documentation was refused for 28 seconds earlier, answered HTTP 200 with real ranked AWS documentation and isError false. This is the control that makes the sibling finding a finding about NAMES rather than about a broken or key-gated tool: the endpoint's prefixed tools work for an anonymous caller exactly as the vendor documents, and only the tool names written into the tool descriptions are wrong. It is filed as its own record because a probe is one request; the record it controls names it by id.
